Stamp Duty Land Tax - Residential property rates. You usually pay Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) on increasing portions of the property price when you buy residential property, for example a house or flat. The amount you pay depends on:. • when you bought the property. • how much you paid for it. • whether you’re eligible for relief or an exemption. Rates for a single property. You pay SDLT at these rates if, after buying the property, it is the only residential property you own. You will usually pay 5% on top of these rates if you own another residential property. Rates from 1 April 2025. Property or lease premium or transfer value SDLT rate. Up to £125,000 Zero. The next £125,000 (the portion from £125,001 to £250,000) 2%. The next £675,000 (the portion from £250,001 to £925,000) 5%. The next £575,000 (the portion from £925,001 to £1.5 million) 10%. The remaining amount (the portion above £1.5 million) 12%. Example. In April 2025 you buy a house for £295,000. The SDLT you owe will be calculated as follows:. • 0% on the first £125,000 = £0. • 2% on the second £125,000 = £2,500. • 5% on the final £45,000 = £2,250. • total SDLT = £4,750. 4 BEDROOM EXTENDED DETACHED FAMILY HOME. THE PROPERTY ALSO BENEFITS FROM A LOW-MAINTENANCE REAR GARDEN, PURPOSE-BUILT STORAGE OUTBUILDING AND OFF-ROAD PARKING. Situated in a popular and established residential location in Erdington, this attractive dormer bungalow offers particularly versatile accommodation, making it an excellent purchase for a variety of buyers. The property occupies a particularly desirable position along a private, unadopted and tree-lined road, offering a peaceful setting with a distinctly rural feel, almost reminiscent of a country lane. With no through traffic or pedestrian access for non-residents, the road enjoys an exceptionally quiet and secluded atmosphere, making it one of the most peaceful locations in the Erdington area. The private road arrangement is an important feature for prospective purchasers to be aware of. The property is approached via a paved front garden with a gated entrance and benefits from an area of off-road parking situated opposite the front entrance, which forms part of the property's ownership. Internally, the accommodation begins with a welcoming entrance hallway providing access to the ground-floor rooms. The front lounge is a good-sized reception room featuring a decorative fireplace, while there are two ground-floor bedrooms, including a rear bedroom with wood-effect flooring and an adjoining snug area. The snug provides useful additional living space and features patio doors opening directly onto the rear garden, together with an attractive glass feature window separating it from the bedroom. The ground floor also includes a fully tiled wet room bathroom, fitted with a shower, wash basin and WC. The fitted kitchen offers a good range of wall and base units, a central island incorporating the sink, a double oven, four-ring gas hob and extractor hood, together with space for additional appliances. A separate utility room provides further practical space and leads to a useful downstairs WC, which also houses the gas combination boiler. From the kitchen, a staircase leads to the first floor where the third bedroom is located. This is a well-proportioned room with a rear-facing double-glazed window and useful eaves storage. Externally, the rear garden has been designed for ease of maintenance, with paved and manageable areas, enclosed boundaries and useful side access. In addition, there is access available to the rear of the property via a passageway running behind Hammond Drive, offering further potential access to the garden. There is also a substantial purpose-built outbuilding at the bottom of the garden, providing excellent additional storage space. The property is conveniently positioned for a range of local shops, supermarkets and everyday amenities, with further shopping and leisure facilities available in Erdington and Sutton Coldfield town centres. There are schools for children of various ages within the surrounding area, together with nearby public transport services and Erdington railway station, providing connections towards Birmingham and beyond. The property is also well placed for access to the A38, providing convenient road links into Birmingham city centre and the wider motorway network. A spacious and versatile dormer bungalow offering a great deal of accommodation, useful outside space and the considerable attraction of an exceptionally peaceful, tree-lined private road setting, all within a convenient Erdington location. text: Situated within the highly regarded sought-after coastal village of Mullion, this spacious, well presented three bedroom home is being offered for sale chain-free. Offering generous and versatile accommodation, this property is ideally suited for family living or those seeking a property in a desirable part of Cornwall. The property also presents an excellent opportunity for buyers looking for a potentially straight-forward purchase. The accommodation comprises of a sitting room, dining area, separate kitchen, conservatory and a garage on the ground floor along with three bedrooms and a bathroom on the first floor. A particularly useful addition is the conservatory, creating an additional reception space and an ideal spot to relax and enjoy the garden throughout the seasons. To the outside, the property benefits from both front and rear gardens. The sizeable front garden is predominantly laid to lawn, providing an attractive approach to the property, whilst the enclosed rear garden offers a pleasant outdoor space for relaxing, gardening or entertaining. A garage and driveway provide convenient off-road parking and additional storage. Combining spacious accommodation, attractive gardens, a garage and driveway parking with an enviable village location close to the Cornish coastline, this property offers an excellent opportunity to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle in one of Cornwall's most desirable locations. An early viewing is strongly recommended. Colroger Close is situated within the popular and well established village of Mullion - one of the largest and most sought-after villages on the beautiful Lizard Peninsula in South Cornwall. Offering a wonderful balance of village convenience, community atmosphere and access to the spectacular Cornish coastline, Mullion is an excellent location for those looking to enjoy a relaxed coastal lifestyle. The village itself offers a good range of everyday amenities, including local shops, convenience stores, cafés, traditional Public Houses, restaurants and independent businesses. There are also primary and secondary schooling facilities, a health centre and pharmacy together with a variety of community groups and recreational activities. A particular attraction of the area is its beautiful surrounding coastline, with miles of scenic coastal walks and an abundance of picturesque beaches and secluded coves close by. Mullion Cove is a charming historic harbour, cared for by the National Trust, nestled beneath rugged cliffs and offering wonderful coastal scenery. Nearby Polurrian Cove and Poldhu Cove are particularly popular, with sandy beaches, opportunities for surfing, swimming and coastal walks along the renowned South West Coast Path. For a wider range of retail, leisure and commercial facilities, the nearby market town of Helston is approximately five miles distant, offering supermarkets, high street retailers, restaurants, leisure facilities and further schooling options. The location also provides a convenient base for exploring the wider Lizard Peninsula, including its picturesque villages, unspoilt countryside and renowned beauty spots. Combining excellent village amenities with easy access to some of Cornwall's finest beaches and coastal scenery, Mullion remains a particularly desirable location for families, retirees and those looking to embrace the very best of coastal living. SITUATION AND DESCRIPTION Occupying a truly exceptional waterfront position in the heart of the highly sought-after village of Bere Ferrers, this fascinating three-bedroom period home enjoys superb, uninterrupted views across the River Tavy towards the far banks. Rich in character and local history, the property combines wonderfully generous accommodation with a setting that is difficult to rival. Believed to date back more than 200 years in part, the property was originally three separate cottages, with the three original entrances still identifiable on an old photograph of the property – two positioned to the front and a third to the side, accessed from the road. For many years it played an important role within village life as the local shop and Post Office, before subsequently being converted to create the spacious and comfortable single home seen today. Its history remains very much part of its charm, with exposed beams, stonework, fireplaces and other period details found throughout. The accommodation is particularly generous, extending to approximately 1,791 sq ft, with three substantial reception rooms providing a great deal of versatility. The main sitting room is an impressive space, measuring approximately 19'7" x 14'4", with a characterful exposed stone wall and fireplace housing a wood-burning stove creating an attractive focal point. The fireplace also retains its original Cloam oven, a particularly interesting reminder of the property's age and history. From here, the property's wonderful position beside the river can be fully appreciated, with the outlook across the water providing an ever-changing backdrop. The dining room is another excellent-sized reception space and continues the character of the house, again benefiting from a wood-burning stove and exposed overhead beams. A further living room provides a third generous reception room, making the ground floor exceptionally flexible for entertaining, family life or those requiring a separate study or snug. The kitchen is positioned alongside the dining room and is fitted with a range of units and work surfaces. Completing the ground-floor accommodation is a useful shower room. Upstairs, the generous proportions continue with three well-sized bedrooms. The two principal bedrooms are particularly spacious, while the third is also a comfortable double room. Several rooms enjoy the property's remarkable outlook, taking full advantage of its position overlooking the river and surrounding landscape. A family bathroom completes the first-floor accommodation. Outside, immediately to the rear of the property is a small enclosed courtyard, providing a private and easily accessible space for outdoor dining, relaxing or enjoying a morning coffee. A small garden shed is positioned at the rear of the courtyard, providing useful additional storage. In addition, the property benefits from a separate parcel of garden situated just a few yards from the front door beside the reedbeds. This provides a further outdoor space in which to sit and enjoy the surroundings. The location is undoubtedly one of the home's defining features. For those looking for something genuinely individual, this is a rare opportunity to acquire a historic village home of considerable character and proportions, positioned right on the waterfront with spectacular views across the River Tavy. Bere Ferrers is an attractive waterside village situated on the Bere Peninsula between the Rivers Tavy and Tamar, surrounded by beautiful countryside and estuary scenery. The village has a strong sense of community and is a small village with a charming, old-fashioned pub which serves homemade food, railway station, café/shop and historic riverside church. There is a social club and a Saturday Market in the village hall where one can buy local produce. The unspoilt surroundings of the Tamar Valley with its rolling hills, meandering rivers and ancient woodlands are ideally suited to those who enjoy walking, riding and water sports and is ideal for sailing enthusiasts with a nearby sailing club and moorings. There are countryside walks and beautiful landscapes to admire within moments of leaving the door, including Dartmoor National Park, which is around 20 minutes by road. Perfect for those who enjoy being away from the bustle of modern life without being disconnected, Bere Ferrers benefits from its own railway station on the picturesque Tamar Valley Line. Bere Ferrers railway station is sited at the top of the village and goes directly into Plymouth within 20 minutes, then onto Exeter and in turn into London Paddington, which can be reached in around 4 hours. Situated 1.5 miles away is the village of Bere Alston which has a wide range of shopping facilities as well as a post office, doctors’ surgery, chemist, and a highly rated primary school. The village is situated approximately 6 miles from Tavistock and about 10 miles from Plymouth. There is a regular train service to and from Plymouth and a regular bus service to and from Tavistock. Occupying an idyllic and private location, Braeface Farmhouse is a traditional stone built property under a pitched slate roof, with several chimney stacks, and finished with a white render. The house is finished to a high standard throughout with a traditional feel while retaining the warmth of a family home. The Kitchen is the heart of this home with ample worksurface and a range cooker, the large dining table is excellent for entertaining, while the sitting area adjoined is perfect to sit in and appreciate the view. The Family room is the cosiest room in the house with log burner on, perfect for enjoying some television. The sunroom connects the property with outside especially in the warmer weather. The principal room is located off the hall from the formal lounge, it enjoys a 27m² footprint, dual aspect allowing natural light in abundance, walk in closet and ensuite bathroom. The second bedroom is at the rear of the property with its own large dressing area, separate bathroom and dual aspect windows. Both upstairs bedrooms are doubles sharing a bathroom. The ground floor also benefits room a large storage room, W.C, utility and storage barn which also grants access to the car port. Garden. The property is set within a generous garden which extends to approximately 2 acres and is mostly laid to lawn enclosed by some shrubs and trees to the south and west. There is a large gravel driveway to the east of the property which provides ample space for parking vehicles. Buildings. The buildings at Braeface Farmhouse comprise:. Log store (9.50m x 8.30m). Of traditional stone construction under a pitched slate roof with a concrete floor. There is a small lean-to extension to the front of the building of timber and steel construction under a felt roof. Bothy (3.80m x 3.00m). Of stone construction under a pitched slate roof with a concrete floor. Additionally, there are equestrian facilities which are situated just to the north of the farmhouse, briefly they comprise:. Timber Stable Block (21.50m x 4.85m) + (7.33m x 4.85m). The land is situated to the south of the farmhouse and is accessed via the main access road and a farm track. Furthermore, ownership of both properties presents the exciting prospect of creating a single substantial residence, subject to the necessary consents. Combining architectural heritage, generous grounds and significant potential, this is an exceptionally rare opportunity to acquire two characterful period cottages in a peaceful and unspoilt rural setting. Rich in history yet offering considerable scope for enhancement, the properties provide an unusual chance from which to create a truly special country home. The property has been thoughtfully improved by the current owner and is offered in excellent decorative order throughout. The spacious hallway provides access to all principal rooms and sets the tone for the light and well balanced accommodation that follows. The master bedroom benefits from built in wardrobes and an en-suite shower room, while a second double bedroom features its own private WC and wash basin. The third bedroom, originally designed as a bedroom but currently used as a dining or reception room, adds flexibility to the layout. A modern family bathroom serves the remaining accommodation. The kitchen is fitted with a range of modern units and includes a breakfast bar, space for appliances, and a door leading to a separate utility room which offers further storage and practical workspace. The sitting room is a comfortable and inviting space with doors that open through to a stunning garden room, a stand out feature of the home. This space was created by upgrading a former conservatory and now boasts a vaulted ceiling with skylights and large windows that frame picturesque views of the rear garden, making it an ideal spot to relax in year round. Outside, the wraparound gardens are a real highlight. Mainly laid to lawn with mature trees, shrubs, and hedging, the garden offers seclusion and a wonderful natural outlook. A timber framed garage and garden shed provide further storage, and there is ample space for additional out buildings or extensions, subject to planning. High Kelling is a charming village that benefits from a shop with a Post Office counter, a doctors` surgery, and a dental practice, while the nearby town of Holt offers a wide range of independent shops, galleries, cafés, and amenities, as well as the renowned Gresham`s School. The North Norfolk coast is just a short drive away, providing access to sandy beaches, coastal walks, and a host of outdoor pursuits. With its combination of location, presentation, and outside space, this bungalow represents a rare opportunity in one of North Norfolk`s most desirable areas. Agents Note. Looking for a detached family home with a woodland backdrop? Tucked away at the rear of a cul-de-sac on George Road in Thetford, this four bedroom freehold home offers living space, a neutral colour palette and a rear garden backing onto established woodland. With two double bedrooms, two singles, an en-suite to the principal bedroom, an integral garage and driveway parking for two cars, it is an attractive choice for growing families. A welcoming hallway leads to the ground floor accommodation, including a cloakroom. The spacious open-plan living and dining area is ideal for relaxing and entertaining, with sliding patio doors opening to the rear garden and drawing in natural light. A separate kitchen overlooks the garden, providing practical cooking space. Upstairs, a large landing provides access to four bedrooms, comprising two comfortable doubles and two singles, suited to children, guests or a home office. The principal bedroom benefits from its own en-suite, whilst a family bathroom serves the other bedrooms. A neutral palette runs throughout, ready for personalisation. Outside, the rear garden enjoys a woodland outlook, whilst a driveway provides parking for two cars alongside an integral single garage. Thetford is a historic Norfolk market town, close to Thetford Forest and surrounding countryside. Residents benefit from local shops, schools, supermarkets and leisure facilities, together with road links via the A11 towards Norwich and Cambridge. The town also has a railway station, making it a practical location for commuters and families seeking town and countryside living. Valuer's Opinion: With four bedrooms, an en-suite, open-plan living space and a woodland outlook, this detached property combines a practical family layout with an appealing cul-de-sac position. The garage and off-road parking are further advantages. Agent's Note: Images may have been digitally enhanced, edited or staged using artificial intelligence and may not reflect the property. Set along North Walsham Road in the peaceful village of Paston, this detached bungalow enjoys an enviable position with sweeping countryside views to the front and a generous plot that provides both privacy and exceptional potential. Requiring cosmetic updating throughout, the property nonetheless offers well proportioned accommodation, a flexible layout and a setting that will appeal to those seeking space, character and the opportunity to add value. Approached via a gravel driveway providing parking for multiple vehicles, the property is framed by a waist-height rendered wall and open rural outlooks that immediately set the tone for the home within its landscape. An entrance porch opens into a central hallway, giving access to the principal rooms. The bedroom accommodation is well balanced, with Bedroom One being a double room to the front featuring a double glazed window and cast iron fireplace. Bedroom Three also sits to the front, enjoying a similar outlook, while Bedroom Two is a large double positioned to the rear with fitted wardrobes and views across the garden. The sitting room forms a versatile central space, featuring a fireplace and excellent flow through the property, with doors leading to Bedroom Two, the internal hallway and French doors opening into the conservatory, creating a bright and connected living arrangement. The kitchen is triple aspect and fitted with hardwood units, offering space for a washing machine and undercounter fridge, with direct access into the conservatory. The conservatory itself provides an excellent additional reception space, complete with an internal water tap, French doors onto the garden and a personal door linking directly into the garage. The bathroom is well appointed with a four piece suite comprising a freestanding roll top bath with Victorian style telephone taps, separate shower cubicle, WC and wash basin, complemented by a heated towel rail and side aspect window. Externally, the property truly excels. The tandem length garage benefits from power, lighting, an up and over front door and rear access into the garden. The rear garden is a particular highlight, beautifully maintained and predominantly laid to lawn with established flower beds, ornamental pond with water feature, storage shed and side access gate, all enjoying a high degree of privacy and open outlooks. Offered with significant potential in a highly desirable coastal-edge setting, this is a rare opportunity to create a bespoke home in a peaceful yet well-connected location. The Local Area:. Paston, Norfolk is a quiet and picturesque coastal edge village set between the market town of North Walsham and the North Norfolk coastline. Surrounded by open farmland and unspoilt countryside, it offers a peaceful rural lifestyle within easy reach of some of the county`s most attractive beaches and coastal walks. Nearby North Walsham provides a comprehensive range of amenities including supermarkets, independent shops, cafés, schools, healthcare services and leisure facilities, while the nearby coastal villages of Bacton and Mundesley offer sandy beaches, clifftop walks and traditional seaside charm. Transport links are excellent for a rural location, with North Walsham railway station offering regular services on the Bittern Line to Norwich, where onward connections to London Liverpool Street are available. The A149 and A140 provide convenient road access across North Norfolk and into Norwich, while Norwich International Airport is within easy reach. This combination of countryside tranquillity, coastal access and strong connectivity makes the area highly desirable for both permanent living and second homes. Notice . The stunning Norfolk coastline, with its beautiful beaches and coastal villages, is also within easy reach, perfect for day trips throughout the year. For those travelling further afield, Hoveton & Wroxham railway station offers regular services into Norwich, where onward connections are available to Cambridge, London and beyond. A handsome four-bedroom period townhouse offering particularly generous and versatile accommodation arranged over three floors, together with a substantial two-storey annexe to the rear. The property retains plenty of the character expected of a home of this age, including an attractive brick façade, sash-style windows, high ceilings and period detailing, while having been updated over the years to provide flexible living accommodation. The ground floor is approached through an entrance hallway, with the principal lounge positioned to the front and featuring an attractive ornate fireplace. Beyond is a separate dining room, providing a useful second reception space, while the kitchen is fitted with a comprehensive range of contemporary gloss units and integrated appliances. A particular feature of the ground floor is the additional family room positioned to the rear. This provides a generous and flexible further living space which could equally function as an additional ground-floor bedroom, with doors opening directly onto the outside area. A shower room completes the ground-floor accommodation. In addition to the main staircase accessed from the entrance hall, a spiral staircase offers access to the first floor from an inner hallway towards the rear of the house. The first floor provides three bedrooms, including two well-proportioned double rooms, one of which benefits from an en-suite, together with the house bathroom. The second floor is home to a particularly generous fourth bedroom, providing useful separation from the remaining bedrooms. In addition to the main house is a separate two-storey annexe situated to the rear. The ground floor provides a substantial open-plan space with its own shower room and kitchenette, while stairs lead to a further large room above. This additional accommodation offers considerable flexibility and could suit a home office, studio, guest accommodation or space for a dependent relative, subject to an individual purchaser's requirements and any necessary consents. Externally, the property has a pleasant paved forecourt to the front, providing space for seating and planting. To the rear is a low-maintenance garden with paved areas, established boundaries and a feature fish pond, providing an attractive outside space situated between the main house and annexe. In summary, this is a substantial period home offering an unusual amount of flexible accommodation for its location, with four established bedrooms and the potential for up to six sleeping areas when incorporating the ground-floor family room and annexe, alongside multiple reception spaces and the considerable benefit of the separate two-storey annexe. LOCATION The property is located within walking distance of York city centre, famed for its historic city walls and York Minster, and offering an excellent range of bars, restaurants, shops and cultural attractions. York's mainline railway station provides regular services to London in under two hours, while good road links make surrounding areas and nearby cities including Leeds and Harrogate readily accessible. The property is also conveniently positioned between two of the city's universities, the University of York and York St John University, as well as being well placed for the wider amenities available across the city centre and surrounding area. A spacious three-storey townhouse offering flexible family living in one of Suffolk’s most well-connected villages. Offering space, versatility and convenience in equal measure, this is a home perfectly suited to modern family life. The Location Red Lodge is a popular and well-connected Suffolk village, ideally positioned between Mildenhall and Newmarket, with excellent access to both the A11 and A14, making it a convenient base for commuters travelling towards Cambridge, Bury St Edmunds, Ipswich and beyond. The nearby railway station at Kennet, approximately two miles away, provides additional transport links, while regular bus services connect the village with surrounding towns and villages. Once a small rural settlement, Red Lodge has grown into a thriving and highly regarded community, offering an excellent balance of countryside living and modern convenience. The village takes its name from the historic Red Lodge Inn, a building dating back to the 17th Century and believed to have once served as a hunting lodge. Today, it remains a popular local venue, known for its restaurant and welcoming atmosphere. For those who enjoy the outdoors, Red Lodge Heath is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest, renowned for its unique landscape and important wildlife habitats. The surrounding Suffolk countryside offers a wealth of walking, cycling and recreational opportunities, whilst nearby Newmarket provides access to the internationally renowned home of British horse racing, complete with racecourses, museums and year-round events. The village itself benefits from a wide range of amenities that continue to grow alongside the community. These include a Primary School, an Ecumenical church, village hall and the well-used Millennium Centre, which hosts various clubs, activities and community events throughout the year. Recreational facilities include tennis courts, sports pitches, a pavilion and allotments, helping to foster a strong sense of community. A modern village centre, opened in 2014, provides convenient day-to-day amenities including a convenience store, pharmacy, takeaway outlets, hair salon and other local services. Residents also benefit from easy access to larger shopping, leisure and healthcare facilities in both Mildenhall and Newmarket. Red Lodge is particularly well regarded for its leisure attractions. Red Lodge Karting is recognised as one of the country's largest karting venues, while nearby Wildtracks Outdoor Activity Park offers a variety of pursuits including archery, motocross, off-roading and other outdoor activities. Together with nearby golf courses, equestrian facilities and nature reserves, the area offers something to suit a wide range of interests and lifestyles.
